identity.name: Ethiopia
alt_names: Provisional Military Government of Socialist Ethiopia

land.text: Ethiopia, liberated from Italian rule in 1941

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Italian Africa shape for 1941 no longer contains Ethiopia; its British Africa shape does.

land.text: the same state restored: the Ethiopian Empire annexed by Italy in May 1936

predecessors.note: The Ethiopian Empire dossier ends in 1936; sovereignty returned in 1941-1942.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page says Ethiopia 'was liberated by the British Army' in 1941, but Cliopatria begins its Ethiopia row in 1942 (the Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement of 31 January 1942 in the infobox) and covers all of the land with its British Africa shape in 1941. The 1942 shape is used for 1941. Reviewer fix: 1941 is drawn as the restored Ethiopia with the ledger's occupation events hatching it: the Ogaden War page says the second Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement of 31 January 1942 ended 'British military occupation in most of Ethiopia except Ogaden', so ledger occupation events cover the whole 1942 shape from 1941, ending in January 1942 for all but the Ogaden and the Haud (to 1948).

1.13 M km2 for 1942-1952, Ethiopia without Eritrea, against the infobox 1,104,300 km2 (no year): ratio 1.02. The Ogaden and Haud are inside the shape but were under British military administration until 1948 (ledger occupation events); the shape stands.

1.25 M km2 with Eritrea, which became a constituent state of the federation on 15 September 1952; infobox 1.10 M km2 for Ethiopia plus Cliopatria's 0.127 M km2 for Eritrea gives 1.23 M, ratio 1.02. Cliopatria starts the shape in 1953; the 1952 gain is in the ledger.
1.25 M km2: the 1953 shape with 900 km2 more on the edge; no page names a border change in 1956.

1.25 M km2 for 1960-1991. The shape holds only to 1990: the war of independence ended in 1991 and Eritrea leaves (ledger 1991, new keyframe 1991). The federation became a province on 15 November 1962 with no change of border; the Ogaden War of 1977-1978 left the border unchanged.

New keyframe: 'Eritrea fought a war of independence from 1961 until 1991'; the 1992 shape (Ethiopia without Eritrea) is used for 1991, a year earlier than Cliopatria. The de jure independence follows the April 1993 referendum.
1.13 M km2 for 1992-2013 against the infobox 1,104,300 km2 (ratio 1.02). Badme and the border zone are inside the shape although awarded to Eritrea in 2002 (ledger occupation events).

1.13 M km2, same as 1992 within 600 km2. Western Tigray and the north of the region changed hands during the Tigray War of 2020-2022 (ledger), but those are internal or occupation changes the shape does not show.
1.13 M km2, the 2014 shape for the last year.

region.text: Ethiopia without Eritrea, liberated in 1941

ledger.note: 1941: Ethiopia is liberated from Italian rule and the Ethiopian state is restored. 'In 1941, during World War II, it was liberated by the British Army.' The page does not name Haile Selassie's return; it dates the Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement to 31 January 1942 (infobox) and 'full sovereignty' to December 1944. Cliopatria draws Ethiopia from 1942 and covers all of it with British Africa in 1941. British military occupation of most of the country lasted to the second Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement of 31 January 1942 (ledger occupation events).

region.text: Ethiopia without the Ogaden and the Haud, under British military occupation

ledger.note: 1941: most of Ethiopia is under British military occupation after the liberation. The Ogaden War page gives only the end: the second Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement of 31 January 1942 ended 'British military occupation in most of Ethiopia except Ogaden'; the Ethiopia page says only that the country 'was liberated by the British Army' in 1941. The start year is bridged from the liberation (page silent on the month).

region.text: the Haud and the Ogaden under British military administration

ledger.note: 1941: the Ogaden stays under British military administration. 'After Italy's defeat in WWII, the Ogaden came under British military administration'; the page gives no year for its start (page silent), and in 1948 'Ethiopian administration resumed in Jigjiga for the first time in 13 years'. 1941 is bridged from the liberation.

region.text: Ethiopia without the Ogaden and the Haud, under British military occupation

ledger.note: 31 January 1942: the second Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement ends British military occupation in most of Ethiopia. The Ogaden War page dates the agreement to 31 January 1942 and says it ended 'British military occupation in most of Ethiopia except Ogaden'; the Ogaden and the Haud stay under British military administration to 1948.

region.text: the Haud and the Ogaden returned by the British

ledger.note: 1948: the British hand the Ogaden and the Haud back to Ethiopia. 'The British gave the Haud and the Ogaden regions to Ethiopia', and 'Ethiopian administration resumed in Jigjiga'. The page elsewhere says 'In the mid-1950s, Ethiopia for the first time controlled the Ogaden'; it does not mention a 1954 handover of the Haud. Ogaden War page, re-read in the reviewer round: 'The last remaining British controlled parts of the region were transferred to Ethiopia in 1955' and the British handed over officials between May and July 1948; the 1955 sentence does not say which parts, so the Haud and the Reserved Area may have been held longer than 1948 (unsettled).

region.text: Eritrea, a constituent state of the federation

ledger.note: 15 September 1952: Eritrea joins Ethiopia in a federation. 'Eritrea formally became a constituent state of the federation of Ethiopia and Eritrea on 15 September 1952', after the British Military Administration (placed over Eritrea in April 1941, 'British Administration' from 1949) ended; 'In December 1950, the UN General Assembly passed Resolution 390 A (V)'. Eritrea keeps its own constituent-state status until 1962; Cliopatria draws it as plain Ethiopian land from 1953.

region.text: Eritrea, where the war of independence was fought

ledger.note: 1 September 1961: armed resistance begins. 'Hamid Idris Awate began armed resistance on 1 September 1961, marking the start of the Eritrean War of Independence.' The Eritrean Liberation Front had been 'established in Cairo in July 1960'. The pages name no rebel-held area, so all of Eritrea is drawn as the zone until 1991 (the researcher's reading); the fronts (ELF, EPLF) need rebel dossiers.

15 November 1962: the federation ends and Eritrea becomes a province. 'On 15 November 1962, the Eritrean Assembly voted unanimously to dissolve the federation and incorporate Eritrea into the Ethiopian Empire as a province.' The border does not change; armed resistance had begun on 1 September 1961 (start of the Eritrean War of Independence).
12 September 1974: the Derg deposes Haile Selassie. 'Haile Selassie's rule ended on 12 September 1974, when he was deposed by the Derg.' The monarchy is abolished in March 1975 (next entry).

March 1975: the monarchy is abolished. The page dates the abolition of the monarchy to 'March 1975'; it names no new official name for the state until the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia in 1987.

region.text: the Ogaden, invaded by the Somali National Army and the Western Somali Liberation Front

ledger.note: July 1977: Somalia invades the Ogaden. The Somali National Army 'committed to invade the Ogaden on July 12, 1977' (infobox: 13 July 1977); 'Gode was captured by the Somalis on July 25'; 'Within less than a month of the invasion, 70% of the Ogaden had been taken'; Jijiga fell on 12 September 1977 and 'Ethiopia was forced to admit that it controlled only about 10% of the Ogaden'. Drawn as one contested zone rather than as occupation because the lines moved through the war.

region.text: the Ogaden, held by Ethiopia again

ledger.note: March 1978: Ethiopia regains the Ogaden. 'The war was effectively concluded with the recapture of Jijiga on March 5'; Barre 'ordered the SNA to retreat into Somalia on 9 March 1978'; on 23 March 1978 'the Ethiopian government declared that the last border post had been regained'. The infobox lists no formal border change.
1987: the Derg dissolves itself and founds the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia. 'In 1987, the Derg dissolved itself and established the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (PDRE).'

region.text: Eritrea, where the war of independence was fought

ledger.note: 1991: the war of independence ends. 'From 1961 until 1991, Eritrea fought a 30-year war of independence against Ethiopia'; the EPRDF overthrew the Derg in 1991 (the page gives no month and does not mention the fall of Asmara), a 1991 agreement let the EPLF 'set up an autonomous transitional government in Eritrea and organize a referendum', and 'This referendum was held in April 1993'. The loss event of 1991 hands the land to the State of Eritrea.

region.text: Eritrea, independent in fact from 1991 and by referendum in April 1993

ledger.note: 1991: Eritrea leaves Ethiopian rule. 'Eritrea fought a war of independence from 1961 until 1991, and the EPRDF overthrew the Derg in 1991'; the referendum followed in April 1993 ('In April 1993, Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia after a national referendum', Ethiopia page). Cliopatria draws the separation from 1992; the dossier follows the page's 1991 for the de facto end.

May 1991: the EPRDF takes power and the Derg regime falls. 'EPRDF forces advanced on Addis Ababa in May 1991'; 'Following the dissolution of the Derg in 1991, the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) dominated the country.' The page gives no exact day.

1995: Ethiopia becomes the Federal Democratic Republic. The infobox gives the constitution as '21 August 1995'; the body says 'In 1994, a new constitution was written' (disagreement); the state is then the 'Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (FDRE)' with '12 regions and two city administrations'.

region.text: the Ethiopian-Eritrean frontier, where the fighting took place

ledger.note: 6 May 1998: Eritrea attacks at Badme and the war begins. 'On 6 May 1998, a large Eritrean mechanized force entered the Badme region'; 'On 13 May 1998, the Ethiopian parliament declared war on Eritrea.' The page names Badme, Zalambessa and an air attack on Assab, not a boundary, so the zone is a band along the frontier.

region.text: Badme, the border town and flashpoint of the war

ledger.note: February 1999: Ethiopia retakes Badme and holds it. 'Ethiopia's forces retook Badme in the February 1999 offensive'; the infobox: 'Ethiopian occupation of disputed territories and the border town of Badme until the 2020 Tigray War'. The Boundary Commission awarded Badme to Eritrea in April 2002 (the page gives 13 or 14 April); Ethiopia did not hand it over. By the end of May 2000 'Ethiopia occupied about a quarter of Eritrea's territory'; the page does not say when that land was returned.

region.text: the Ethiopian-Eritrean frontier

ledger.note: 12 December 2000: the Algiers peace agreement ends the war. 'On 12 December 2000 a peace agreement was signed by the two governments'; the parties agreed to a peace agreement and binding arbitration on 18 June 2000, and a 25-kilometre Temporary Security Zone was set up inside Eritrea (Resolution 1312, 31 July 2000).

region.text: Badme, the border town

ledger.note: 2020: Ethiopia's hold on Badme ends. The infobox gives the Ethiopian occupation of Badme and the disputed territories as lasting 'until the 2020 Tigray War'; the page names no month. Peace between the two states was declared in July 2018 and the Ethiopian ruling coalition agreed on 5 June 2018 to implement the 2000 agreement.

region.text: the Tigray Region

ledger.note: 3 November 2020: the Tigray War begins. The war 'lasted from 3 November 2020'; Tigrayan forces attacked Northern Command bases just before midnight on 3 November, and federal allied forces captured Mekelle on 28 November. Zone: the Tigray Region.

region.text: northern Tigray along the Eritrean frontier

ledger.note: November 2020: Eritrean forces enter northern Tigray. 'Amhara and Eritrean forces also controlled parts of Tigray in the west and north, respectively'; 'Eritrean forces later controlled much of the northeast'. The year is read from the war's start; the page gives no month for the entry. The region is the part of Tigray along the Eritrean frontier, the researcher's reading. Western Tigray was taken by Amhara regional authorities, an internal change inside Ethiopia.

region.text: most of the Tigray Region without the Eritrean-held north and without Western Tigray, held by Amhara regional authorities (gazetteer name 'Western Tigray' still to be added); held by the TDF from late June 2021

ledger.note: 28 June 2021: the Tigray Defense Forces retake Mekelle and hold most of Tigray. 'On 28 June 2021, the Tigray Defense Forces retook the city of Mekelle'; Ethiopia then declared a unilateral ceasefire; late June 2021: the International Crisis Group said 'the TDF now controlled most of the Tigray region'. Reviewer af-01-c: confidence lowered to 2 because the region includes Western Tigray, which the Tigray War infobox says was 'ceded and occupied by neighboring Amhara regional authorities' from November 2020. Reviewer round: Western Tigray (Amhara-held from November 2020: 'Within the same month, Amhara Region forces took over and occupied Western Tigray') is now subtracted by name (gazetteer entry 'Western Tigray' to be added).

region.text: the Awra and Chifra districts of Afar near the Amhara border

ledger.note: 17-19 July 2021: the TDF attack into Afar. 'From 17 to 19 July, the TDF began launching attacks in the Afar Region to its east'; on 13 October 2021 fighting 'resumed in Afar, within the Awra and Chifra districts near the Amhara border'; 'Heavy fighting in western Afar displaced over 54,000 people'. The page speaks of attacks and fighting, not of captured towns, so the Afar edge is the researcher's reading of the land the TDF held (page silent on the extent).

region.text: Lalibela and Weldiya in North Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: August 2021: the TDF take Lalibela and Weldiya. 'The next day, Lalibela was reported to have been seized by Tigrayan forces' (the sentence before is dated 4 August 2021); 'the city of Weldiya was captured by the TDF on 12 August 2021'. Amhara Region land outside the Tigray contest zone.

region.text: Dessie and Kombolcha in South Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: 30-31 October 2021: the TDF take Dessie and Kombolcha. 'On 30 October, it was reported that Dessie had fallen to the TDF'; 'On 31 October, the TDF claimed to have captured Kombolcha, a town 21 km (13 mi) east of Dessie'.

region.text: the Awra and Chifra districts of Afar near the Amhara border

ledger.note: 20 December 2021: the TDF withdraw from Afar and Amhara. 'On 20 December 2021, the TPLF announced they had withdrawn their troops from Amhara and Afar'.

region.text: Lalibela and Weldiya in North Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: December 2021: Lalibela and Weldiya are no longer held. The Ethiopian government said it had 'recaptured several towns in the Amhara and Afar regions including Lalibela and Shewa Robit' (26 November-6 December 2021); the page gives no date for Weldiya; 'On 20 December 2021, the TPLF announced they had withdrawn their troops from Amhara and Afar'. December is the page's date of the withdrawal.

region.text: Dessie and Kombolcha in South Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: 6 December 2021: government forces retake Dessie and Kombolcha. 'On 6 December, government forces claimed to have recaptured the strategic cities of Dessie and Kombolcha.'

region.text: Shire (Inda Selassie), the strategic city of western-central Tigray

ledger.note: 17 October 2022: federal and Eritrean forces take Shire. 'that same day, the strategic city of Shire was taken by Eritrea and Ethiopia, leading to the evacuation of thousands of its inhabitants'; the TDF had entered Shire on 30 June 2021 'after it had been abandoned by Eritrean troops'. The 50 km radius is the researcher's reading; the Eritrean share is part of the occupation of the north (ledger 2020).

region.text: the Tigray Region

ledger.note: 2 November 2022: the Pretoria cessation of hostilities. Ethiopia and the TPLF 'signed an agreement for a cessation of hostilities', effective 3 November; Eritrea 'were not involved in the agreement'.

region.text: the TDF-held part of Tigray after the loss of Shire in October 2022: Tigray without the Eritrean-held north, without Western Tigray (Amhara-held) and without Shire

ledger.note: 23 March 2023: Tigray returns under a federal Interim Regional Administration. The infobox: 'Interim Regional Administration of Tigray formed on 23 March 2023'; the page does not say who held Tigray's land between the cessation of hostilities and that date, so the month is the formation of the administration. Reviewer round: the region now matches the TPLF dossier's loss of the same month (Tigray less the Eritrean-held north, Western Tigray and Shire).

region.text: northern Tigray along the Eritrean frontier

ledger.note: 2024: the Eritrean occupation of northern Tigray is closed at the last year of the data. The page says only that Eritrea 'largely continued to occupy parts of Tigray as of 2023' and gives no end date (page silent).

wars.name: Eritrean War of Independence
wars.outcome: Eritrea separates: the war ends in 1991 with the EPRDF's overthrow of the Derg, and Eritrea becomes independent by referendum in April 1993.
wars.note: 'Hamid Idris Awate began armed resistance on 1 September 1961, marking the start of the Eritrean War of Independence'; the Eritrean-Ethiopian War page: 'Eritrea fought a war of independence from 1961 until 1991'. The pages name no rebel-held area, so the contest events (September 1961 to 1991, counterpart 'Eritrean independence fighters') draw all of Eritrea as the zone; a rebel dossier for the Eritrean fronts (ELF, EPLF) is needed.

wars.name: Ogaden War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian-allied victory: Somali forces take 70% of the Ogaden within a month and about 90% by late September 1977, then are driven out between January and March 1978; no formal border change.
wars.note: 13 July 1977 to 23 March 1978 (infobox). Soviet support shifts to Ethiopia; Cuban forces 12,000-18,000; Dire Dawa and Harar hold.

wars.name: Eritrean-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian military advantage: Ethiopia occupies 'about a quarter of Eritrea's territory' by May 2000; the Algiers Agreement of 12 December 2000 and the Boundary Commission's ruling of April 2002 award Badme to Eritrea, but Ethiopia holds it until the 2020 Tigray War.
wars.note: 6 May 1998 to 25 May 2000 (Ethiopia declared the war over); the page gives the Commission's ruling as 14 April 2002 in the text and 13 April 2002 in the references.

wars.name: Tigray War
wars.outcome: Cessation of hostilities signed 2 November 2022 in Pretoria; Western Tigray ceded to and occupied by Amhara regional authorities; Eritrea 'largely continued to occupy parts of Tigray as of 2023'; an Interim Regional Administration formed 23 March 2023.
wars.note: The TDF retook Mekelle on 28 June 2021 and advanced into Afar and Amhara (Weldiya, 12 August 2021) before withdrawing, announced 20 December 2021.

certainty.note: The pages opened fix no frontier by survey: the Ogaden frontier with Somalia is provisional; after independence 'the border became an international frontier' and the two governments 'could not agree on where it should be drawn'; the Boundary Commission ruled in April 2002 and Ethiopia did not implement the ruling.

notes: Page budget up to 5 pages, five used (Ethiopia, Federation of Ethiopia and Eritrea, Ogaden War, Eritrean-Ethiopian War, Tigray War). Not reached within the budget: the Eritrean War of Independence and the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (a rebel state that held land before 1991), the Anglo-Ethiopian Agreements of 1942 and 1944, the 1954 handover of the Haud and the Reserved Area, the 1964 Ethiopian-Somali border war, the Ilemi triangle. Cliopatria's Ethiopia row begins in 1942 (the Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement of 31 January 1942); the page says the country was liberated in 1941 and that 'full sovereignty' returned with the agreement of December 1944 (the infobox gives 31 January 1942), so the dossier starts in 1941 with a new keyframe and Cliopatria's British Africa row, which holds all of Ethiopia in 1941, should be trimmed by the British Africa dossier. The Ogaden is shown inside Ethiopia throughout; Britain administered it (with the Haud) to 1948 per the Ogaden War page, which also says 'in the mid-1950s, Ethiopia for the first time controlled the Ogaden' (disagreement). Eritrea: the 1952 federation is drawn as plain gain (Cliopatria's shape), not as vassal land; the 1962 change is a status caption. Eritrea's separation is dated 1991 (war ended) while Cliopatria and the State of Eritrea row use 1992; the referendum is April 1993 (no day on the pages). The 'identity.end' 2026 is only the current year; the Cliopatria row ends in 2024. Rulers are omitted: the pages give only fragments (Haile Selassie to 12 September 1974, Mengistu head of state from 11 February 1977, Meles Zenawi to 20 August 2012, Abiy Ahmed from 15 February 2018). Ethiopia-Tigray: Western Tigray taken by Amhara regional authorities is an internal change inside Ethiopia and not in the ledger; the Tigray People's Liberation Front dossier (rebel) carries the rebel side. Counterparts needing dossiers: tigray-people-s-liberation-front (written by this batch), the Eritrean liberation fronts. Gazetteer names needed: Haud (region), Badme (place). Reviewer round (af-01-c-fixed): added (1) British military occupation of most of Ethiopia 1941 to 31 January 1942 (Ogaden War page: the second Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement ended it 'in most of Ethiopia except Ogaden'), the Ogaden and the Haud staying occupied to 1948 as before; (2) contest events for the Eritrean War of Independence, September 1961 to 1991, zone all of Eritrea, counterpart 'Eritrean independence fighters' (rebel dossiers needed for the ELF and EPLF); (3) TDF occupation of Amhara and Afar land in 2021, split into three spans by what the Tigray War page dates: the Afar edge (attacks from 17-19 July, confidence 1), Lalibela and Weldiya (August), Dessie and Kombolcha (30-31 October), all ended by 20 December 2021, mirrored in the TPLF dossier; (4) Shire taken on 17 October 2022; (5) Western Tigray subtracted by name from the 2021 loss and the 2023 gain, which now use the TPLF dossier's regions (gazetteer names needed: Western Tigray, Weldiya, Kombolcha, Chifra, Shire). The Ogaden War page also says 'The last remaining British controlled parts of the region were transferred to Ethiopia in 1955', which the dossier does not resolve.
